messages.subject: how to capture df data
parts:
Hi all,

I am looking at the package fitbitScraper and it works fine within Deducer.

This is a package to retrieve one's Fitbit data and I want to compare two persons sleep which would be easy to do in Deducer with plots and the work on testing correlations on what might make sleep better.
When I am using Deducer for my  bat research data everything is straight forward as the data is in a format that can be seen in the data viewer and saved.

What I can not figure out is how to capture the varied data that is retrieved from Fitbit in the df so I can plot, compare and then run some correlations on the data?
This example is only 2 nights and one person, but would like to save the data each type so I can work with it later.

Sample below

Tnx for any help

Bruce

messages.subject: Re: how to capture df data
parts:
I have not worked with this data before, but it looks like a list with a data.frame as an element, so you should be able to do something like:

sleep <- get_sleep_data(cookie, start_date="2017-06-06", end_date="2017-06-07”)
sleep_df <- sleep$df



Ian
